summary: Remote WebSocket server can drive an interactive PTY shell on the installer's host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent is a long-running agent that opens a WebSocket connection to a configurable server (SERVER_URL env /.claude-agent.json / systemd unit) and dispatches server-originated messages into privileged local sinks. The `terminal_input` message type writes attacker-controlled bytes directly into a spawned interactive PTY (bash/pwsh/cmd via pty.spawn using process.env.SHELL), giving the party that controls the WebSocket endpoint a full-host interactive shell on the installer's machine. Additional message types perform file writes, git operations, and an `upgrade_agent` handler that shells out to `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restarts the process via systemd user unit, launchd plist, or PM2 — providing a server-initiated code-update and restart channel. The `yeaft-agent install` subcommand writes `~/.config/systemd/user/<service>.service` with `WantedBy=default.target`, enabling and starting the unit so the remote-controllable agent auto-starts on every login and survives reboots. The remote-shell, remote-upgrade, and persistence surfaces together constitute a backdoor whose blast radius equals whoever holds the configured server URL.
